home.headline: At these figures, the deposit and buying costs are in place around July 2028.
assumptions: Showing first-time-buyer rates; a 30-year mortgage with a €35,000 deposit (10%); a €350,000 home, as given; not a new build, so no Help to Buy and standard rates (a BER C where a lender prices by BER); stamp duty of €3,500 (1%) and €3,000 for legal fees and a survey (an estimate); costs compared over the first 5 years for every lender: interest on a 30-year term plus the valuation fee, less cashback paid within 5 years and any savings bonus; a shorter fix moves to its stated follow-on rate for the rest of the 5 years.
home.sortedBy: 49 options that fit, sorted by cost over the first 5 years, lowest first (another order can be chosen).

conditions: 4 Year Fixed HVM BER C is for loans of €250,000 or more.

MortgageSaver: €2,000 less DIRT, paid into the account within 5 working days of a Bank of Ireland first-time-buyer mortgage being drawn down in full: €200 to €2,500 a month by direct debit for 6 months in a row, €5,000 or more saved and still held at drawdown, within 30 months of opening. One bonus per mortgage; one account per person; can be held alongside SuperSaver.
The bonus is paid after drawdown, so it lowers the cost rather than the deposit needed: the keys date is the same.

presentation: At these figures, the deposit and buying costs are in place around July 2028.

Showing first-time-buyer rates; a 30-year mortgage with a €35,000 deposit (10%); a €350,000 home, as given; not a new build, so no Help to Buy and standard rates (a BER C where a lender prices by BER); stamp duty of €3,500 (1%) and €3,000 for legal fees and a survey (an estimate); costs compared over the first 5 years for every lender: interest on a 30-year term plus the valuation fee, less cashback paid within 5 years and any savings bonus; a shorter fix moves to its stated follow-on rate for the rest of the 5 years.
49 options that fit, sorted by cost over the first 5 years, lowest first (another order can be chosen).

moneyFound.basis: A year’s figures, after DIRT at 33%: idle cash against the best confirmed instant-access rate (only where its current rate was given), debt interest not paid in the next twelve months less what the same money would earn, and a mortgage switch’s lower repayment. Bonuses, cashback and rates resting on CCPC’s one figure are not counted. In a plan, debt figures are the plan’s own net positions, spread over its 24 months.

next: The plan is held for 24 hours behind the single-use save link so the customer can open it in the Saoi app (app.saoi.ie), then deleted unless opened; nothing else is stored. Offer the link. In the app the plan opens as a card, and Saoirse, Saoi’s assistant, knows it and can talk it through; signing in with an email address keeps it across devices, including the installed app. Alerts when a chosen product’s rate changes and reminders as the goal date nears are coming, not built yet.
